newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Navan says buys Spanish mine for $3.43 mln.
newsitem.headline: Navan says buys Spanish mine for $3.43 mln.

text.p: Navan Resources Plc said on Tuesday it acquired Minas de Almagrera SA for $3.43 million from SEPI, a government company, as part of the Spanish Government's privatisation programme.

Navan will also assume $5.3 million in debt as part of the deal, it said in a statement. Half of the consideration will be paid on signature of the agreement with the second tranche of $1.71 million payable after the auditing of the transfer balance sheet, the capital restructuring of Almagrera and the receipt of the formal ratification by The Privatisation Transparency Board and the council of ministers, Navan said.
These steps are expected to take three months.
Almagrera made a loss of $4.63 million for the year ended 31 December, 1995 on sales of $34 million.
Navan said the plant is capable of treating in excess of one million tonnes of polymetallic ore a year from Almagrera's Sotiel and Migollas mines.
Almagrera is situated 20 km from Navan's Aguas Tenidas orebody and Navan said the acquisition will substantially reduce both the cost and the time required to develop this project.
"Output at Calanas can be increased, and unit operating and overhead costs reduced, by combining the two operations," Navan Resources said in a statement.
